## Scope and coverage

Read-only source review of the exact JSON diagnostics and enclosing functions. No builds, tests, formatters, linters, or validation commands were run. The JSON accounting is complete: 20 SIMD reports and 21 zmath reports. This is not a clean-sweep claim: the independent latest `std.zig.Ast.parse` probe recorded 54 parser failures (`parser-coverage.stderr` / `ast-check.json`), including SIMD `src/formats/xml.zig` (later parse failure at line 3456) and one unrelated zmath file. ZBC currently does not surface those parser failures, so coverage outside the supplied JSON is partial.

Classification totals: 40 confirmed false positives; 1 plausible real bug requiring runtime validation. No actual project bug is claimed.

## Root cause A — path-sensitive nonzero proof missing in `index-minus-one-without-zero-guard` (17 SIMD reports)

All 17 are **confirmed false positives**. The indexed subtraction is dominated by a loop, short-circuit, or parser-state invariant that proves the operand is nonzero.

- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/core/json_lexical.zig:196` — **confirmed false positive**. `feed` enters the block only under `while (local_offset < input.len)`. It computes `valid_count = @min(VLEN, input.len - local_offset)`, therefore every call to `processStrictBlock` has `valid_count >= 1`; `[valid_count - 1]` is safe.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/core/json_lexical.zig:321` — **confirmed false positive**. Same `feed` loop and same `valid_count` invariant for `processDialectBlock`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/core/json_lexical.zig:619` — **confirmed false positive**. `updateOrdinarySpan` starts with `if (start >= end) return;`; the later `bytes[end - 1]` is reached only with `start < end`, hence `end >= 1`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/xml.zig:380` — **confirmed false positive**. `scanXmlLexical` runs under `while (cursor < input.len)`, then sets `block_end = @min(cursor + VLEN, input.len)`. Thus `block_end > cursor >= 0`; the `candidate_count == 0` branch cannot index `block_end - 1` at zero.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/xml.zig:465` — **confirmed false positive**. Same `scanXmlLexical` loop invariant on the `!rescan` tail path.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/xml.zig:708` — **confirmed false positive**. `isCommentTerminatorAt` first rejects `input_index < comment_start_offset` and then rejects `input_index - comment_start_offset < 6`; the indexed path therefore has `input_index >= 6`. Its caller also runs under `while (input_index < input.len)`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:1085` — **confirmed false positive**. `InlineParser.parsePlain` uses `self.pos > start and self.owner.input[self.pos - 1] == ' '`; short-circuit evaluation proves `self.pos > 0` before the subtraction.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:1414` — **confirmed false positive**. `trimCommentEnd` uses `index == start or input[index - 1] == ' '`, so the second operand is evaluated only when `index > start`, which implies `index > 0`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:1451` — **confirmed false positive**. `findBlockColon` has the same `index == start or input[index - 1]` short-circuit proof.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2328` — **confirmed false positive**. `YamlParser.parsePlain` uses `(pos == start or self.input[pos - 1] == ' ')`; the indexed operand is evaluated only for `pos > start`, hence `pos > 0`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2584` — **confirmed false positive**. In the sequence branch, `if (self.block_len == 0 or self.block_frames[self.block_len - 1].indent < line.indent)` pushes a frame and returns when `block_len == 0`. Reaching the following `self.block_frames[self.block_len - 1]` access proves `block_len != 0`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2599` — **confirmed false positive**. Identical control-flow fact in the mapping branch: the zero-length case pushes a frame and returns before the indexed access.

- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2636` — **confirmed false positive**. Same `.sequence_value` frame invariant after `parseScalar`.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2664` — **confirmed false positive**. Same frame invariant for `.mapping_value` when the value is empty.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:2682` — **confirmed false positive**. Same frame invariant for `.mapping_value` after `parseScalar`.

**Minimal repro candidates:**

```zig
while (cursor < input.len) {
    const end = @min(VLEN, input.len - cursor);
    _ = input[end - 1];
}

fn f(bytes: []u8, start: usize, end: usize) void {
    if (start >= end) return;
    _ = bytes[end - 1];
}

if (self.block_len == 0 or self.frames[self.block_len - 1].indent < indent) {
    self.push();
    return;
}
_ = self.frames[self.block_len - 1];
```

**Recommended rule/infrastructure boundary:** extend the existing `src/flow/value_range.zig` facts beyond named variables. It must preserve relational facts (`start < end => end >= 1`), `@min` lower bounds, short-circuit disjunctions, and state-machine facts established by a branch that returns after `pushBlock`. Do not add source-name suppressions for `block_len`, `valid_count`, or `input_index`; the proof must be path-sensitive and under-approximating.

## Root cause B — valid nullable pointer-to-optional out-parameters (2 SIMD reports)

Both are **confirmed false positives** for `double-optional-ptr`.

- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:1130` — **confirmed false positive**. `external_failure: ?*?Failure` is an optional pointer to an optional failure result. The body uses `const failure: *?Failure = external_failure orelse &local_failure;` and passes it to validators. This is the intended nullable out-parameter shape.
- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/formats/yaml.zig:1170` — **confirmed false positive**. Same type is used by `parseYamlIndex`; callers create `var failure: ?Failure = null`, pass `&failure`, and write `target.* = source_failure` / `target.* = reason` on error.

The exact semantics are not duplicated optionality by accident: the outer `?` says “caller may omit the output”; the inner `?Failure` says “the output may contain no diagnostic”.

**Minimal repro candidate:**

```zig
fn parse(input: []const u8, external: ?*?Failure) void {
    var local: ?Failure = null;
    const out: *?Failure = external orelse &local;
    _ = input;
    out.* = null;
}
```

**Recommended rule boundary:** do not report `?*?T` from type shape alone. Suppress when the function uses the optional pointer as an out-parameter (`if (p) |target| target.* = ...`, or `orelse &local`), or redesign the rule to report only when the value is used as a nullable pointer rather than written as an optional result. The current rule's blanket “use `?*T` for nullable out-parameter” rationale is not valid for an optional-result out-parameter.

## Root cause C — borrowed lifecycle capability mistaken for owned resource (1 SIMD report)

- `/tmp/zbc-assessment-6j53ve64/simd/src/core/resident.zig:73` — **confirmed false positive** for `owned-field-no-outer-cleanup`.

Exact evidence: `Guard` is `{ lease: Lease, expected_position: usize }`. `Lease` is `{ state: *State, generation: u64 }`; its `release` method only checks generation and writes `state.active = false` / `state.claimed = false`. The document owns the lease and explicitly calls `lease.release()` in its own `deinit`; guards are copied and used as borrowed iteration capabilities. The resident tests explicitly use `defer lease.release()` while dropping `guard` without a cleanup call.

The detector reaches this result because `src/model/method_names.zig:isCleanupMethodName` classifies the generic method name `release` as cleanup and `owned_field_no_outer_cleanup.zig` treats any non-trivial cleanup method as evidence of ownership.

**Minimal repro candidate:** the `State`/`Lease`/`Guard` trio in `resident.zig`, especially `Lease.release`, `Lease.claim`, and the test pattern `defer lease.release(); var guard = try lease.claim();`.

**Recommended rule boundary:** distinguish owned resource destruction from borrowed capability invalidation. At minimum, model `release` separately from `deinit`/`close`; preferably inspect whether the method frees/owns storage or only mutates a pointee/generation token. A name-only cleanup classification is too broad for lifecycle guards.
